builders.name: Greg Brockman
builders.bio: President & Co-Founder @OpenAI

tweets.text:
I helped start OpenAI because I want AGI to be safe and beneficial for people. This post provides transparency that can be the foundation of industry-wide shared safety bars.

Perhaps the most important concept from the post is the following: "AI will also significantly contribute to progress on alignment and monitoring, I think that progress is unlikely to be fast enough to allow the full potential acceleration in pretraining."

Towards ensuring that safety keeps pace with general intelligence of pretrained models (as measured by "perplexity"), the post proposes "common limits, based on perplexity and other measurements, that developers are committed to not crossing until our ability to understand and monitor AI behavior achieves a certain concrete milestone (such as the development of a successor to CoT monitors)."

The general idea is to create a first shared limit, on some shared key metric, along with concrete exit criteria that would allow going beyond that. This can lead to a "common framework for setting successive limits and pacing further development".

Excited to move forward the conversation on pacing towards shared standards that are rooted in the science!

tweets.text:
Yes to all of this. As agents take on more and more long running project work, and you have swarms of agents that parallelize work against a goal, the agent harness and architecture for orchestration will have to evolve. 

One of the biggest shifts is how those agents collectively share their knowledge, keep track of the tasks, and also coordinate with human users. This in theory is technically straightforward, but there’s a ton of complexity to get right to ensure agents can both get access to the revenant resources without too much or little exposure.

There are a lot of lessons to pull from based on how people already do this kind of work together (people share their files, have computers to work with, community in chats and inboxes, and so on). But equally the primitives need to be able to enable this work at a throughput far higher than people, and in a world where agents can much more easily become a vector of security risk. 

Going to be super fun building out this next generation of how agents operate. Lots of opportunity here both for horizontal and vertical specific approaches to bring this to life.

美联储 2% 的通胀目标，可能真的要守不住了。

亿万富翁、潘兴广场 CEO 比尔·阿克曼最新发文，直言美联储将在 12 月 9 日的议息会议上再次犯错。

他认为，如今的金融环境已经明显收紧，连 SpaceX 这样的投资级公司都需要以 8.259% 的利率进行担保融资，而 IPO 时发行的无担保债券利率还不到 6%。

更重要的是，地缘政治风险、全球军费扩张、逆全球化与关税，以及 AI 基础设施和能源领域的巨额投资，都在持续改变通胀环境。

阿克曼的判断是：2% 的通胀目标已经不切实际，3% 才更符合当下的经济现实。

如果美联储继续加息，试图强行将通胀压回 2%，可能最终把美国乃至全球经济拖入衰退。

当市场还在争论美联储何时降息时，华尔街已经有人开始质疑：美联储是不是从一开始就定错了目标？

AI 股票跌到「便宜得离谱」，但华尔街可能已经没钱继续为 AI 买单了。

Anthropic 创纪录 IPO 未能挽救科技股抛售，市场开始担心 AI 泡沫正在破裂。

Seaport Research Partners 首席股票策略师 Jonathan Golub 在彭博最新采访中却认为，这轮下跌可能已经过度。

他指出，半导体企业的盈利预期仍在持续上调，算力需求没有消失，部分芯片股估值甚至已经低于历史平均水平。

但 Golub 同时提出一个更大的问题：

未来一年，AI 数据中心及相关基础设施可能需要约 1.5 万亿美元融资，其中 9000 亿美元依赖债务。

当科技公司还在不断扩大算力投入，债券投资者却开始要求更高的回报。

AI 的需求或许没有问题，但华尔街还能为这场基建竞赛提供多少资金？

👇 彭博采访精华：Jonathan Golub 谈 AI 股暴跌与融资风险

稳定币市场也开始失血了，年内已有超 300 亿美元撤离。

据 DefiLlama 数据，稳定币总市值已降至 2842.15 亿美元，创年内新低。相比 5 月 17 日的高点 3143.92 亿美元，缩水约 301.77 亿美元，降幅达 9.6%。

更值得关注的是，稳定币总市值在 9 月末曾短暂回升至 3057.98 亿美元，但随后再次掉头向下，过去 30 天又减少了 6.15%。

稳定币是加密市场最重要的流动性来源之一。如今不仅 BTC、ETH 等风险资产持续承压，连场内稳定币资金池也在收缩。

价格下跌可以归因于抛售，但当稳定币供应量也开始持续下降，市场需要面对的可能不只是价格问题，而是流动性问题。
